key_insight: A transverse-field Ising model with a global, non-monotonic time-dependent field can simulate arbitrary quantum circuits with only polynomial overhead, making it polynomially equivalent to the gate model of quantum computation.
engineering_relevance: This connects analog quantum hardware and quantum annealing-style systems to universal quantum computing, while also implying that efficient classical simulation of such driven Ising dynamics is unlikely under standard complexity assumptions.
method: Builds on a global-control result for Rydberg atoms.
Constructs a simulation mapping from arbitrary circuits to the Ising model with global transverse field.
Shows polynomial overhead in time, qubit count, and energy scale.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a constructive theoretical result with polynomial overhead bounds, not an experimental benchmark or numerical dataset.
watch_item: The overheads are described as large, so the construction is not yet practical for near-term hardware or efficient simulation workflows.
paper_title: Polynomial equivalence of the global transverse-field Ising model and the gate model of quantum computation
